name: Ten bad ideas
intent: Outrun the inner critic by demanding badness first.
when: creating, or when the human is blocked by wanting to be good
prompt: {prompt|Ten ideas. Deliberately bad. Speed over quality.}
readback: Read box 10 first. The point is not the ideas but what the human couldn't help writing.

claims.claim: Separating idea generation from evaluation, with judgement deferred until generation is done, increases the number of ideas without reducing, and sometimes increasing, the number of good ones.
Instructing people to generate deliberately bad ideas lowers self-censorship and yields more ideas, including some usable ones, than instructing them to generate good ideas.
claims.construct: lowered quality criterion; instruction effects in divergent thinking

claims.claim: In a single idea-generation run, later ideas tend to be more original than earlier ones.
claims.construct: the serial order effect in divergent thinking

grounding.helps: when wanting a good idea is what stops the first one being written; later ideas in a run tend to be a little more original, a small tendency that is unreliable for any one person, and asking for bad ideas is untested craft, so treat the ten as a warm-up and read the later boxes first
grounding.backfires: when "bad" turns into jokes rather than range, or when ten is too few to get past the obvious answers: the studies of later ideas being more original used timed runs of several minutes
